title: Good Things We OKC! vs. LALALALA: The Middle-Tier Test
summary: OKC edged LALALALA 252.06–233.99 to move to 5–2.
bodyHtml:
OKC Wins a Tight One

Final: Good Things We OKC! 252.06, LALALALA 233.99. Margin: 18.07 points. This was the week's second-closest finish, a matchup that helped define the separation between the upper standings and a crowded middle group. Good Things We OKC! improved to 5–2; LALALALA fell to 3–4 despite putting up a respectable total.

Good Things We OKC!: A Linebacker Leads the Way

Alex Singleton's 34.65 points were the leading IDP performance among the Week 7 defensive standouts, and a major difference-maker in a game decided by fewer than 20. Caleb Williams (22.12), CeeDee Lamb (21.90), Quay Walker (19.50) and Christian McCaffrey (19.00) ensured Singleton's outing had plenty of support.

The final 252.06 was OKC's winning number, and the team's 5–2 record through seven weeks placed it third in the league. The roster has shown it can win with meaningful contributions from both offensive stars and defenders, a useful formula in this league's format.

LALALALA: A Losing Score With Real Quality

LALALALA had standout IDP work of its own. Fred Warner posted 25.00, with Quincy Williams contributing 18.75 and Chase Young adding 16.25. Ollie Gordon II (16.80) and Jaylen Warren (15.20) helped on offense. The team didn't collapse; it simply came up short against a slightly stronger lineup.

At 3–4, LALALALA's record undersells some of its weekly scoring potential: 1,807.02 total points for through Week 7 actually exceeded OKC's 1,801.36. Wins are decided by scheduled opponents, not just cumulative points, and this result drove that point home.

What This Means

OKC protected its upper-tier position, and LALALALA remained close enough to turn things around. The gap between the two was less than one big defensive play's fantasy value. In a league with high-impact IDP scoring, that makes every start/sit call consequential.

title: New York Noodles vs. Utah Yetis: A 102-Point Statement
bodyHtml:
Noodles Turn a Rivalry Into a Rout

Final: New York Noodles 277.67, Utah Yetis 175.28. Margin: 102.39 points. What began as a normal Week 7 matchup ended as the largest blowout on the slate. The Noodles didn't reach the week's top overall score, but they produced more than enough to remain undefeated at 7–0, while Utah fell to 2–5.

New York Noodles: Contributions Everywhere

It wasn't a one-man performance. Drake Maye (27.44) provided quarterback stability, Trey McBride (27.10) delivered at tight end, and Aidan Hutchinson (24.25) gave the defense an anchor. Geno Smith (23.48) and Tykee Smith (21.00) added more strong outings. The Noodles received 152.92 offensive points and 124.75 defensive points, illustrating how difficult this roster can be to contain under the league's IDP-heavy scoring format.

There is one surprising footnote to the convincing win: Yaya Diaby (33.60), Jessie Bates III (26.25) and Jamien Sherwood (23.00) all scored heavily on the bench. The published optimal-lineup analysis estimated 89.45 points left on the bench. It didn't matter against Utah, but that gap is worth monitoring in closer contests.

Utah Yetis: A Difficult Week With Some Bright Spots

Utah's 175.28 was the lowest team total of the five matchups. Still, Patrick Queen's 26.55, Bucky Irving's 23.50 and Rhamondre Stevenson's 20.00 gave the Yetis legitimate contributions. The trouble was the overall depth of the scoring response against a Noodles team that piled up quality starts across positions.

Utah moved to 2–5, with 1,446.63 points for through seven weeks. The goal now is to find a more consistent full-lineup output rather than relying on a handful of strong individual scores.

What This Means

New York's unbeaten streak remains the headline, but this victory was as much about roster balance as star power. Utah has to turn isolated successes into an entire team's worth of production. Both managers will come away with very different reasons to study the lineup decisions from Week 7.

title: Week 7: Blowouts, Bench Regrets and an Unbeaten Leader
summary: HOU led all scorers, the Noodles stayed perfect, and the closest result came down to 11.82 points.
bodyHtml:
Week 7 Around the League

Week 7 offered a little of everything: a team-best scoring eruption, a runaway result, a pair of games decided by fewer than 20 points, and enough unused bench production to make several managers reconsider their Sunday decisions. Across the five matchups, HOU You Like That posted the week's highest score (296.81), while New York Noodles delivered its seventh consecutive win.

All Five Results

  • New York Noodles 277.67, Utah Yetis 175.28 — margin: 102.39
  • HOU You Like That 296.81, Seattle Supersonics 214.57 — margin: 82.24
  • NJz Bunniez 234.97, Dalla Dalla Dallas 223.15 — margin: 11.82
  • Good Things We OKC! 252.06, LALALALA 233.99 — margin: 18.07
  • District of Daebak 225.66, Tampa Bay Tyranny 192.60 — margin: 33.06

The Highs

Top team score: HOU You Like That (296.81). HOU broke through with the largest total of the week behind Joe Burrow (28.88), Tee Higgins (23.80) and Dak Prescott (23.28), alongside useful production from both sides of the ball. The victory over Seattle was emphatic, even as HOU remained 2–5 through seven weeks. That's the kind of ceiling that can change the mood around a difficult start.

The unbeaten standard: New York Noodles (7–0). A 102.39-point victory over Utah was the biggest win by margin. Drake Maye (27.44), Trey McBride (27.10) and Aidan Hutchinson (24.25) headlined a balanced lineup. With 2,124.06 cumulative points through Week 7, the Noodles also led the league in scoring.

Closest escape: NJz Bunniez by 11.82. Tony Pollard's 35.00 points and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 26.80 helped the Bunniez withstand Dallas. Those are substantial contributions in a matchup that still hung close enough for one lineup decision to matter.

The Lows

Dallas had a plausible path to reversing the result. The matchup data identifies a legal linebacker swap — Christian Elliss for Gabe Jacas — worth an estimated 19.25 additional points, more than the 11.82-point loss. This is a hindsight comparison, not a claim that the entire optimal lineup was guaranteed or obvious beforehand.

NJz left a monster score unused. Blake Cashman recorded 53.40 points on the Bunniez bench, the type of individual total that usually takes center stage. They won anyway, which makes this less a costly mistake than an extraordinary what-if.

Tampa's struggles continued. The Tyranny fell to 1–6 after scoring 192.60 against Daebak. Its 1,669.26 points for and 1,884.64 points against through Week 7 demonstrate how challenging the opening stretch has been.

The Standings Picture

At the Week 7 checkpoint, New York Noodles (7–0) and NJz Bunniez (6–1) had established a clear early pace. Good Things We OKC! followed at 5–2. Seattle (4–3) occupied the next tier, while the middle and lower standings still had room to shift as the season progressed. Results, records and player totals here reflect the provided Week 7 Sleeper export and are subject to later stat corrections.

Read the five individual matchup recaps for both sides of every result, the decisive performances, and what each outcome means for the next stretch.

title: HOU You Like That vs. Seattle: A 296-Point Breakout
summary: HOU delivered the highest score of the week, beating Seattle 296.81–214.57.
bodyHtml:
HOU Brings the Firepower

Final: HOU You Like That 296.81, Seattle Supersonics 214.57. Margin: 82.24 points. HOU had been looking for a result to change the conversation around its season. Week 7 provided one in convincing fashion: the highest score in the league this week, handed to a Seattle side that entered the matchup in the upper half of the standings.

HOU You Like That: Quarterbacks Set the Tone

The foundation was a strong two-quarterback combination. Joe Burrow scored 28.88, while Dak Prescott added 23.28. Tee Higgins (23.80), Omar Cooper Jr. (20.00), Boye Mafe (19.85) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (19.70) kept the production flowing. This was not merely an offense running hot; the output included contributions throughout the IDP lineup.

HOU improved to 2–5. That's still a difficult position in the table, but an almost 300-point week shows a ceiling that its record alone doesn't reveal. With 1,701.56 points for through Week 7, the roster has performed better than a quick glance at the win column might suggest.

Seattle Supersonics: Good Performances, Wrong Opponent

Seattle put up 214.57, powered by Luther Burden III (21.70), Nakobe Dean (21.25), Kirk Cousins (20.40) and Jared Goff (18.02). In isolation, these are useful scores. Against HOU's explosion, they weren't remotely enough.

There were also alternatives on the bench, including Malik Willis (26.02) and Keisean Nixon (20.00). The optimal-lineup calculation estimated 53.90 points left on the bench, but even recovering those points would not erase the entire 82.24-point deficit. Seattle slipped to 4–3.

What This Means

HOU now has a benchmark for what its roster can look like when the quarterback and skill-position production align. Seattle must treat this as a setback rather than proof of collapse: sometimes an opponent simply turns in the week's strongest performance. The next test is whether HOU can repeat this level and whether Seattle can return to form.

title: District of Daebak vs. Tampa Bay: A Needed Win
summary: Daebak beat the Tyranny 225.66–192.60 as Tampa fell to 1–6.
bodyHtml:
Daebak Takes Care of Business

Final: District of Daebak 225.66, Tampa Bay Tyranny 192.60. Margin: 33.06 points. Neither team entered the week at the top of the standings, which made this game particularly meaningful. Daebak produced a complete enough lineup to claim its third win; Tampa was left searching for answers after another defeat.

District of Daebak: Defense Supplies the Edge

Quinnen Williams scored 21.80 and DeMarvion Overshown added 21.15, two strong defensive performances that helped Daebak create separation. Cam Skattebo (18.60), Matthew Stafford (17.50), Brandon Jones (17.50) and Jordan Love (16.96) all added to the total.

Daebak reached 3–4 through Week 7 with 1,738.33 points for. Its overall point differential remained positive at the checkpoint, a sign that the squad's record might not tell the whole story about its competitiveness.

Tampa Bay Tyranny: Bright Spots, Insufficient Total

Tampa still had reasons to applaud individual players: Quinshon Judkins scored 22.90, Javonte Williams 21.50, Jordyn Brooks 16.50, and Tucker Kraft 14.80. The problem was the sum. 192.60 was not enough to match Daebak's 225.66.

The Tyranny fell to 1–6 and had allowed 1,884.64 points through seven weeks, the highest points-against total in the provided standings. Some of that is schedule adversity, but the offense also needs additional scoring depth to turn respectable starts into wins.

What This Means

For Daebak, the result keeps a route open to climb above .500. For Tampa, the immediate challenge is simply to build a full-lineup performance that doesn't leave the team dependent on its opponent having an off week. There is still time left in the 17-week season, but the margin for error is narrowing.

title: NJz Bunniez vs. Dallas: Eleven Points and a What-If
summary: NJz survived 234.97–223.15, but a Dallas bench decision looms over the result.
bodyHtml:
The Closest Game of Week 7

Final: NJz Bunniez 234.97, Dalla Dalla Dallas 223.15. Margin: 11.82 points. Four of the five Week 7 games were decided by at least 18 points. This one was the exception. The Bunniez held on to move to 6–1, while Dallas dropped to 2–5 and was left with a particularly painful lineup what-if.

NJz Bunniez: Star Power Makes the Difference

Tony Pollard's 35.00 points were the highest offensive-player total in the provided Week 7 standouts. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.80) supplied another major contribution, while Bobby Okereke (19.75) and Payton Wilson (18.55) offered defensive stability. The Bunniez did enough to secure the win and retain their position directly behind unbeaten New York in the standings.

Yet the biggest individual number associated with NJz never counted toward the final: Blake Cashman scored 53.40 points on the bench. The team's full optimal-lineup analysis estimated 127.90 points left unused. NJz escaped regardless, but this was a reminder of how brutal lineup selection can be in a deep IDP format.

Dalla Dalla Dallas: The One Swap Everyone Will Notice

Dallas had solid production from Bo Nix (26.18), Zay Flowers (23.70), Jameson Williams (23.60) and Colston Loveland (19.90). Its 223.15 total kept the game competitive throughout the final accounting.

The export flags a legal hindsight substitution: Christian Elliss (22.75) for Gabe Jacas at linebacker, worth an estimated 19.25-point gain. Because Dallas lost by 11.82, that single change would have been enough to flip the result, all else equal. It is easy to identify the move after the games have ended; the manager still had to make the choice before knowing the final scores.

What This Means

NJz remains in the title chase at 6–1, but Dallas can reasonably feel that an attainable win got away. This was the league's narrowest Week 7 margin and arguably its most memorable bench story. For both sides, better lineup optimization could make an even bigger difference in future close games.
